# [AMD] Qwen3-Next: consume the fused AR+norm+quant output

**Depends on #39140** (the Gluon kernel) and **#44565** (the FFN-side wiring).
It targets `main` independently rather than stacking: until those land the
declarations here are inert rather than harmful — the attention side falls
through to the existing aiter path and the FFN read is ignored.

Last of three. This is the PR that changes behaviour for a model, and the only
one with end-to-end numbers.

## What this does

Declares the quantized read on the Qwen3-Next decoder layers so the boundary
hands down `(bf16, fp8, scale)` instead of a tensor, and routes the pieces to
the consumers that can take them:

* `declare_attn(read=NormQuantReadout(...))` on both decoder layers —
  `Fp8Input.TUPLE_AND_BF16` for the GDN layer, whose small `in_proj_ba` gating
  projection needs bf16 alongside the quantized `in_proj_qkvz`, and
  `Fp8Input.TUPLE` for the attention layer.
* `_forward_input_proj` and the `qkv_proj` sites unpack the tuple, giving each
  linear the member it can consume.
* `Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock` routes the MLP side, keeping `qwen2_moe.py` —
  shared by several models — byte-identical to upstream.

Every declaration is conditional on the consuming projection actually accepting
an FP8 tuple, so a build whose projections are not block-quantized keeps the
plain AR+RMSNorm path.

## The FFN read is not installed unconditionally

`declare_ffn` defaults to `NORM_READOUT`, and `NormQuantReadout` is not a
drop-in substitute: on an empty batch `NormReadout` keeps the previous residual
while `NormQuantReadout` returns `hidden_states` as the residual. `_ffn_read()`
therefore returns `NORM_READOUT` unless `_use_aiter` is set **and** the MoE
block can consume an `(fp8, scale)` pair, so no other backend sees a changed
declaration.

The attention side needs no equivalent: `declare_attn` already defaults to
`NORM_QUANT_READOUT`, the same type, so `fp8_input=None` there is the default.

## Scope

The kernel serves `M ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8, 16}` at hidden 2048, TP4, eps 1e-6, on
gfx950 with `SGLANG_USE_AITER`. Above M=16, aiter's
`allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group` is as fast or faster, so
`is_supported()` declines and the existing path serves the shape. Anything
outside the envelope — other architectures, other TP sizes, CUDA — is
unaffected.

## Results

4× MI355X (gfx950), TP4/EP1, `Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct-FP8`, ISL/OSL
1024/1024, un-profiled, shared-expert fusion at its default (on). Baseline is
the same commit with none of these three PRs applied. Output tok/s:

| C ≈ decode batch | stock | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 227.5 | 235.4 | **+3.5%** |
| 2 | 434.7 | 446.3 | **+2.7%** |
| 4 | 843.7 | 869.2 | **+3.0%** |
| 8 | 1641.0 | 1682.6 | **+2.5%** |
| 16 | 2989.9 | 3077.7 | **+2.9%** |
| 32 | 4769.5 | 4822.0 | **+1.1%** |
| 64 | 7327.0 | 7508.3 | **+2.5%** |

GSM8K 1319q: **0.946**, `Invalid: 0.000`, against 0.948 for stock — within
run-to-run spread (readings across arms ranged 0.941–0.948).

The two PRs below this one are measured as no-ops on the same hardware: the
kernel alone is within ±0.1% of stock at every concurrency, and the wiring
within ±0.5%. The gain appears only when a model declares the read, which is
what this PR does.

Measured with #42483 cherry-picked, because Qwen3-Next does not currently start
on `main` without it; this branch does not carry that commit.

## Test plan

* GSM8K 1319q against stock at the same commit.
* Output-throughput sweep at C = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64.
* Kernel-vs-aiter isolation arm, to attribute the delta between the kernel and
  the declarations.

## Hardware

gfx950 (MI355X), TP4, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`.

+def _linear_accepts_fp8_tuple(linear: nn.Module) -> bool:
+    quant_method = getattr(linear, "quant_method", None)
+    return quant_method.__class__.__name__ == "Fp8LinearMethod" and (
+        getattr(quant_method, "block_quant", False)
+        or getattr(quant_method, "use_mxfp8", False)
+    )
+
+
+def _select_fused_ar_input_for_linear(hidden_states, linear: nn.Module):
+    """Pick the member of a fused-AR output tuple that ``linear`` can consume."""
+    if not isinstance(hidden_states, tuple):
+        return hidden_states
+    if len(hidden_states) == 3:
+        hs_bf16, hs_fp8, hs_scale = hidden_states
+        if _linear_accepts_fp8_tuple(linear):
+            return (hs_fp8, hs_scale)
+        return hs_bf16
+    if len(hidden_states) == 2 and _linear_accepts_fp8_tuple(linear):
+        return hidden_states
+    raise TypeError(
+        f"{linear.__class__.__name__} cannot consume fused AR quant tuple input"
+    )
+
+
+class Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock(Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock):
+    """MoE block that can consume the fused AR+norm+quant tuple.
+
+    With ``Fp8Input.TUPLE_AND_BF16`` declared on the FFN stage the boundary
+    hands down ``(bf16, fp8, scale)``. Where the fp8 goes depends on whether
+    the shared expert was fused into the routed experts:
+
+      * fusion off -- the separate shared expert's FP8 ``gate_up_proj`` takes
+        ``(fp8, scale)``;
+      * fusion on  -- the routed experts take it via ``pre_quant_input``,
+        which covers every expert rather than just the shared one.
+
+    The router gate, the shared-expert gate and the MoE's own bf16 inputs are
+    untouched. Subclassing keeps ``qwen2_moe.py``, shared by several models,
+    byte-identical to upstream.
+    """
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        hidden_states,
+        forward_batch: Optional[ForwardBatch] = None,
+        defer_finalize: bool = False,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        if not isinstance(hidden_states, tuple):
+            return super().forward(hidden_states, forward_batch, defer_finalize)
+
+        hs_bf16, hs_fp8, hs_scale = hidden_states
+        shared = getattr(self, "shared_expert", None)
+        restore = []
+
+        if shared is not None:
+            if not _linear_accepts_fp8_tuple(getattr(shared, "gate_up_proj", None)):
+                return super().forward(hs_bf16, forward_batch, defer_finalize)
+            original = self._forward_shared_experts
+
+            def shared_with_fp8(hidden, apply_gate: bool = True):
+                # Gates stay on bf16; only the FP8 projection sees (fp8, scale).
+                shared_output = self.shared_expert((hs_fp8, hs_scale))
+                if self.shared_expert_gate is not None and apply_gate:
+                    shared_output = (
+                        torch.sigmoid(self.shared_expert_gate(hidden)) * shared_output
+                    )
+                return shared_output
+
+            self._forward_shared_experts = shared_with_fp8
+            restore.append(("_forward_shared_experts", original))
+        elif _routed_experts_accept_pre_quant(self):
+            # The runner declines the hand-off (wrong quant layout, router
+            # weights pre-applied) by ignoring pre_quant_input, so this is safe
+            # to offer unconditionally once the backend is known to read it.
+            experts = self.experts
+            for name in ("forward", "forward_deferred_finalize"):
+                bound = getattr(experts, name, None)
+                if bound is None:
+                    continue
+                restore.append((name, bound, experts))
+                setattr(
+                    experts,
+                    name,
+                    partial(bound, pre_quant_input=(hs_fp8, hs_scale)),
+                )
+        else:
+            return super().forward(hs_bf16, forward_batch, defer_finalize)
+
+        try:
+            return super().forward(hs_bf16, forward_batch, defer_finalize)
+        finally:
+            for entry in restore:
+                if len(entry) == 2:
+                    setattr(self, entry[0], entry[1])
+                else:
+                    setattr(entry[2], entry[0], entry[1])
+
+
+def _routed_experts_accept_pre_quant(mlp) -> bool:
+    """Whether the routed-expert runner can take caller-quantized activations.
+
+    Always False for now. The plumbing works -- FusedMoE.pre_quant_input reaches
+    the runner and the aiter standard pre-permute can forward it -- but aiter's
+    heuristic then selects an asm kernel that this gfx950 build does not carry:
+
+        fmoe_fp8_blockscale_g1u1 failed: get_heuristic_kernel not find kernel
+        gfx950_..._fmoe_bf16_blockscaleBf16_g1u1_vs_pf2_silu_16x128
+
+    aiter's own mori path carries an upscale fallback for exactly this class of
+    gap. Until a build ships that kernel, declining keeps the fp8 unproduced
+    rather than produced and discarded, which measured as a net regression.
+    """
+    return False
+
+
+def _moe_accepts_fp8_tuple(mlp) -> bool:
+    """True when this MLP can consume (bf16, fp8, scale) somewhere downstream.
+
+    Two shapes, depending on shared-expert fusion:
+      * fusion off -- a separate ``shared_expert`` whose FP8 ``gate_up_proj``
+        takes ``(fp8, scale)`` directly;
+      * fusion on  -- no separate shared expert, so the fp8 goes to the routed
+        experts via ``pre_quant_input``.
+    """
+    if not isinstance(mlp, Qwen3NextSparseMoeBlock):
+        return False
+    shared = getattr(mlp, "shared_expert", None)
+    if shared is not None:
+        return _linear_accepts_fp8_tuple(getattr(shared, "gate_up_proj", None))
+    return _routed_experts_accept_pre_quant(mlp)
+
+
+def _ffn_read(mlp, is_layer_sparse: bool):
+    """The FFN stage's read declaration.
+
+    ``declare_ffn`` defaults to ``NORM_READOUT``, and ``NormQuantReadout`` is
+    not a drop-in substitute for it: on an empty batch the former keeps the
+    previous residual while the latter returns ``hidden_states`` as the
+    residual. Install the quantized read only when the fp8 will actually be
+    consumed, so every other backend and model keeps the stock behaviour.
+    """
+    if not (_use_aiter and is_layer_sparse and _moe_accepts_fp8_tuple(mlp)):
+        return NORM_READOUT
+    return NormQuantReadout(fp8_input=Fp8Input.TUPLE_AND_BF16)
+

+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.layer_boundary.residual.add_norm import (
+    NORM_READOUT,
+    Fp8Input,
+    NormQuantReadout,
+    NormReadout,
+)
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _PlainAdd:
+    """The update object the boundary passes when the producer adds plainly."""
+
+    is_plain_add = True
+
+
+class TestEmptyBatchResidual(CustomTestCase):
+    """NormQuantReadout is not a drop-in replacement for NormReadout.
+
+    They diverge on the empty-batch path: NormReadout keeps the residual it was
+    given, NormQuantReadout returns hidden_states as the residual. Installing
+    the quantized readout unconditionally therefore changes behaviour for every
+    backend, not only the one the fused kernel runs on.
+    """
+
+    def _read(self, readout, hidden_states, residual):
+        return readout.update_and_read(
+            _PlainAdd(), hidden_states, residual, norm=lambda *a: None
+        )
